title: KiroCrew App Store editorial feed
description: Everything about how the store PRESENTS apps: the category taxonomy, which apps are in which category, and the Discover layout. Only REFERENCES apps by name -- app data always resolves through the registry, so editorial can never inject a phantom or spoofed app. Read tolerantly: unknown section types are skipped, and a section that fails validation is dropped individually rather than failing the page.

schemaVersion.description: Integer major. Additive-only within a major: new fields are optional and existing fields never change meaning. A major the client does not support triggers FULL fallback (cache -> bundled snapshot -> built-in heuristic), not a partial render.

minClientVersion.description: Independent of the schema major. Lets the server force older clients onto their bundled default when a doc relies on behavior they lack. A client below this ignores the document entirely.

categories.description: Taxonomy AND membership together, so the reference check (`appRefs` -> a declared app) is the same cross-document check the publish step already runs for sections, and the registry carries no presentation at all. `order` drives the rail sequence -- there is no separate ordering section. An app in no category falls into a default bucket and is never hidden; membership is single-valued by construction (an app appearing in two categories is a curation error the publish step rejects), because a partitioned rail is the whole point -- use a `rail` section for cross-cutting collections instead.

sections.description: Ordered Discover layout. Data-driven, not a fixed template -- new layouts are new `type` values, which is what lets the store's appearance change without a client release.

appRef.description: Must resolve to a live, non-tombstoned entry in the merged registry. The publish pipeline enforces this; the client drops the reference if it does not resolve.

label.description: Display string. Relabeling is a catalog edit, not a client release -- which is why nothing references a category by label.

order.description: Required, because an absent order has no defined placement: uniqueness can only be checked among the values that are present, so a category without one would land wherever array position happened to put it.

section.description: Closed per known variant, but the CLIENT must skip an unrecognized `type` rather than reject the document. Validating strictly here is for the publish gate; the reader is deliberately more tolerant.

sectionRail.title: rail -- titled group, for CROSS-CUTTING collections
sectionRail.description: Independent of the taxonomy: this is how an app appears in more than one place without multi-category membership ("Staff picks", "New this month").

md.description: Restricted markdown. Rendered through the dashboard's sanitizer -- never raw HTML.

href.description: https only. A curated feed must not be able to point the client at other schemes.
